HxResult HxHtmlViewDelete ( HxHtmlView_t *  pHtmlView  ) 

Delete a HTML viewer widget.

HxHtmlViewDelete deletes a HTML viewer created from an earlier call to HxHtmlViewNew.

It is not necessary to call this function when quitting the application, since the widget's parent calls this function just before the parent is deleted. HxHtmlViewDelete only needs to be called when removing a HTML view at runtime.

This will delete the container that holds the HTMLView, so there's no need to call HxContainerDelete after calling this.

Parameters:
pHtmlView IN: Pointer to the container to delete
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxHtmlViewInit ( void   ) 

Initialize the HTML Viewer library.

This function is called to initialize the HTML Viewer library in offline mode where only file:// URL access is allowed. It isn't normally needed, as HxHtmlViewNew will init the library if it hasn't been used before, but it can be called to shift init time earlier in the program.

Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails.

HxResult HxHtmlViewInitOnline ( void   ) 

Initialize the HTML Viewer library in "online" mode.

This function is called to initialize the HTML Viewer library, giving it access to the Intetnet connection to load additional data. This is used for programs where the library needs to have access to the external web. Due to limitations in the HTML library, this online/offline flag is set on a per-library basis and can only be set when the library is first loaded.

Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails.

HxResult HxHtmlViewNew ( HxContainer_t *  pContainer,
HxHtmlView_t **  hHtmlView 
)

Create a HTML viewer widget.

This function is called to turn a HxContainer_t widget into an HxHtmlView_t. The widget now acts like a mini-web browser that is embedded within a window or dialog. Unless the library has already been initialized with HxHtmlViewInitOnline, this browser window will be limited to offline (file-system) content.

Parameters:
pContainer IN: Container that will hold the HTML View
attr IN: One or more HxHtmlViewAttributes_t flags
hHtmlView OUT: Handle to the created HTML viewer
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails, and sets *hHtmlView to NULL.

HxResult HxHtmlViewShowFile ( const char *  pFilename,
const HxRectangle_t *  pBounds,
const char *  pTitle,
const char *  pButtonLabel1,
const char *  pButtonLabel2,
const char *  pButtonLabel3,
uint32_t *  pSelectedButton 
)

Show a HTML file in its own dialog.

This function is similar to the alert APIs, but instead of showing a text string and icon, a HTML file is rendered into the window. The command buttons all will dismiss the dialog. If no URI (file:// or http://) prefix is used, the path is assumed to be the absolute file name.

pSelectedButton in an input and output argument. For input, it signifies which command button has initial focus. For output, it communicates which command button was selected by the user. The value of 0 represents the leftmost command button, while a value of 1 represents the second command button. If pSelectedButton is NULL, or if the input value of pSelectedButton is more than (number of command buttons - 1), then the initial focus is given to the leftmost command button. The output value of pSelectedButton is not defined if HxHtmlViewShowFile does not return HX_OK.

Like alerts, the rightmost command button is used as the escape button (i.e., pressing the Delete key acts on this button).

Parameters:
pFilename IN: String containing full pathname to HTML file or URL to show. See HxHtmlViewSetLocation for an example.
pBounds IN: Position and size of the dialog to display or NULL for default size
pTitle IN: Title of HTML dialog, or NULL
pButtonLabel1 IN: String for first command button
pButtonLabel2 IN: String for second command button, or NULL
pButtonLabel3 IN: String for third command button, or NULL
pSelectedButton IN/OUT: Pointer to number of selected command button or NULL if information not needed. Defaults to the left most button.
